sources.title: Mohammed Dahleh, Munther A. Dahleh, and George Verghese, Lectures on Dynamic Systems and Control, Chapter 25: Minimal State-Space Realization

contents.name: The finite observability matrix and the unobservable kernel directions
contents.locator: §25.2, the unobservable subspace defined by the kernel of the stacked C, CA, ... matrix and its output consequence, PDF pp. 3–4; the local theorem proves the finite-horizon iff and least-squares bound independently

contents.name: An unobservable mode can be removed without changing the input-output realization
contents.locator: §25.2, decomposition and unobservable subspace, PDF pp. 3–4; the example supplies its own explicit diagonal two-state calculation

contents.name: Discrete-time state-space model, Markov-parameter indexing, and realization convention
contents.locator: §25.3, equations (25.10)–(25.12), PDF p. 5; the local convention indexes M_k=CA^kB and states that this is one sample after an impulse

contents.name: A state-coordinate similarity gives the same transfer function and impulse response
contents.locator: §25.3, PDF pp. 5–6; the local proof covers arbitrary common inputs and arbitrary matched initial states by induction

contents.name: Two different state-coordinate matrices produce the same outputs under all common inputs
contents.locator: §25.3, coordinate-change relation, PDF pp. 5–6; the example supplies its own explicit 2 by 2 matrices

contents.name: Minimal realizations are similar; the proof uses equality of observability-controllability Hankel products and full-rank pseudoinverses
contents.locator: §25.4, Theorem 25.3 and complete proof, PDF pp. 7–8; the local finite-Hankel theorem is separately proved for fixed q and exact Markov parameters

contents.name: An exercise points to a Markov-parameter construction when the minimal order is known
contents.reason: The exercise does not provide its complete algorithm or proof. The local algorithm and fixed-window similarity argument are proved in full and do not treat the exercise as a supplier.

sources.title: Sanjay Lall, Engr207c: Operator Theory and Linear Systems, State-Space Realization lecture notes

contents.name: Discrete-time state recurrence and impulse-response indexing
contents.locator: §9.2, state recurrence and impulse-response formula, PDF p. 3; the local definition states its exact horizon, noise, and one-index convention

contents.name: The finite observability matrix maps the initial state to the future output stack
contents.locator: §9.2, PDF p. 6, equations relating y_future and O x(0); the local proof also derives the forced-response subtraction and the least-squares error bound

contents.name: State-coordinate changes preserve transfer functions, impulse responses, and common-input outputs
contents.locator: §9.2, PDF pp. 3–4, coordinate change and state recurrence

contents.name: A visible two-state coordinate change preserves the entire common-input output sequence
contents.locator: §9.2, coordinate-change interpretation, PDF pp. 3–4; the worked matrices are locally computed

contents.name: An unobservable state component lies in the kernel of every finite observability stack
contents.locator: §9.2, unobservable space and observability matrix, PDF pp. 3–4; the worked diagonal example is locally computed

contents.name: Hankel factorization by observability and controllability matrices, with the rank comparison proof
contents.locator: §9.2, Theorem 8, Corollary 9, and the subsequent interpretation, PDF pp. 5–6; the local proof derives the finite factor identities and similarity matrix directly

contents.name: Hankel matrices as a route to data-based realization
contents.locator: §9.2, Hankel-matrix realization context, PDF p. 6; the notes do not specify the local exact rank-d thin-SVD and pseudoinverse procedure, which is fully defined locally

contents.name: Scalar canonical-form and entrywise transfer-function construction procedures
contents.reason: These procedures do not implement the local block-Hankel SVD algorithm. No correctness or stability claim is transferred from them.
